title: MediaPlayer.create returns a non-null PREPARED player; instance methods follow the AOSP state table
statement: MediaPlayer.create(Context, resid) never returns null for a valid resource (it throws on failure) — it returns a player in the PREPARED state. start/pause/stop/release/reset transition per the class-doc state table; illegal transitions log and enter ERROR (mirrors the C++ audio::MediaPlayer table). The engine allocates a real heap object with __mp_state__; audio OUTPUT is a no-op in a software runtime. Without this object law, every app whose onClick plays a sound before acting dies silently on a deferred null-receiver NPE (F-155).
test: fishrings S10 chain at HEAD: 3 taps → 3 CLICK dispatches → 3 rotations → 3 distinct board states, deterministic x2; MediaPlayer NPE count 1/tap → 0
